question: How is the chance that an event actually causes harm different from the chance that someone starts it?
preregistered_evidence: regardless of the magnitude of harm that can be expected
a1_answer:
The likelihood of initiation or occurrence refers to the probability that a threat event will be started or happen, while the likelihood of impact addresses the probability that the event will result in an adverse impact [nt-043]. These two distinct probabilities are combined to determine the overall likelihood of the threat event [nt-044].

[nt-043] [nt-044]
a2_answer: The likelihood of impact addresses the probability that a threat event will result in an adverse impact, regardless of the magnitude of harm, while the likelihood of initiation or occurrence addresses the probability that the event will be started or happen [nt-044]. These two distinct components are then combined to determine the overall likelihood of the threat event [nt-044].
guide_expected_answer: Likelihood of initiation/occurrence = the chance a threat event is started (adversarial) or occurs (non-adversarial). Likelihood of impact = the chance that, once initiated or occurring, it results in adverse impact, regardless of the magnitude of harm. The overall likelihood combines the two.
guide_required_points: States that one likelihood is that the event is initiated/occurs. || States that the other is that, once initiated, it results in adverse impact (not the size of the harm). || (Completeness) mentions that the overall likelihood combines the two.
guide_qualification: The likelihood of impact is about whether harm results, 'regardless of the magnitude of harm' (it is not the severity).
guide_acceptable_wording: Any faithful paraphrase; 'probability' and 'chance' are interchangeable.
guide_unsupported_claim_examples: Describing the likelihood of impact as the severity or size of the harm. || Swapping the two definitions. || Stating that the two are multiplied or combined by a specific formula (the guide specifies no algorithm; see also N1).
guide_supporting_passages: nt-044: The likelihood of impact addresses the probability (or possibility) that the threat event will result in an adverse impact, regardless of the magnitude of harm that can be expected. || nt-042: The likelihood risk factor combines an estimate of the likelihood that the threat event will be initiated with an estimate of the likelihood of impact || nt-144: Second, organizations assess the likelihood that threat events once initiated or occurring, will result in adverse impacts to organizational operations and assets
guide_grader_notes: Preregistered gold nt-043 + nt-044; overlay v1.1 also accepts nt-042 and nt-144 as independently sufficient and treats nt-043 as a partial fragment.

a2_answer: No, the risk level is typically not higher than the impact level, but impact as an upper bound on risk may not hold when addressing organization-wide issues or when multiple risks materialize concurrently or repeatedly [nt-153]. guide_acceptable_wording: 'does not always hold', 'may fail to apply'.
guide_unsupported_claim_examples: Answering yes / 'always capped'. || Claiming likelihood can push risk ABOVE the impact level (the source says likelihood can reduce risk below impact). || Giving specific numeric thresholds or levels not in the passages.
